# #1797: Patch: the AI's search keeps a play's placements apart when they differ only in lane, so trying every lane is not undone
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
When the practice AI considers playing a unit, it is meant to try every lane that would make a difference: next to a friendly unit, away from an enemy that hits neighbours, or opposite a particular card. But a duplicate check later in its search treats two boards as the same when the only difference is which lane a unit stands in. So it throws away every such lane but the leftmost before it can compare them. In practice, the AI only chooses lanes well when the lane changes something immediately. Otherwise it takes the first open spot, even when that spot is next to the unit an enemy with Cleave is about to hit. Once built, it keeps those placements and can choose between them.

## Why
- The search's root tries a play in every distinct placement (#1635; `crates/ai/README.md:72-73`, `config.rs:91-97`, `root_candidate_set` at `candidates.rs:557-561`). Placements are told apart by `placement_key` (`candidates.rs:75-97`), which reads the neighbours and the lane's four zones.
- The beam then drops an open child whose `search_signature` it has already seen (`search.rs:209-215`). That signature leaves a unit's lane out on purpose: "A unit's lane is left out, so the two lanes `candidate_actions` keeps for one play stay one position" (`simulate.rs:835-836`). The unit part (`simulate.rs:863-879`) has no slot.
- Units are signed in board order. With one friendly unit in lane 1, a new unit in lane 2, 3 or 5 signs the same `[old, new]` every time, and only lane 2 survives.
- So the every-placement root helps only cards whose lane changes the board at once, like Lane Eater and Mushroom Power in the #1635 tests.
- It doesn't help placements whose worth shows later, even though the evaluation can see them: the imagined enemy reply prices Cleave damage to neighbours (`reply.rs:96-107`, `AI_REPLY.cleave_share`).
- #1635's own screen read 197-203, an edge of -0.015 (`config.rs:96-97`). That fits most of its new placements never reaching the comparison.

## Proposal
- Give the beam's duplicate check a placement-aware signature: add each unit's lane, or its own-side neighbours, to the unit part. Use it for the beam's `seen` set only. The lethal solver's visited set (`lethal.rs:230`, `:244`) keeps today's signature, so its cost doesn't grow.
- Stop lane variants that score the same from filling the beam (`beam_width` 4). Either keep one open child per play and score, or cap a play's lane variants in the frontier at `AI_SEARCH.zone_variants`.
- Any new number is a named constant in `config.rs` (CLAUDE.md rule 9).

## Where it lands
- `crates/ai/src/simulate.rs` (the signature), `crates/ai/src/search.rs` (the beam's duplicate check)
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/search.rs` (`mod lanes_that_play_differently`), `crates/ai/README.md`
- §3.1 (lanes and adjacency), §6 Cleave, §9.9 (the AI)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Search test: an enemy Cleave attacker is on the board, one AI unit stands in lane 1, and a vanilla unit is in hand. `beam_search`'s lines include the vanilla placed in a lane not next to the friendly unit.
- [ ] `decide` test: in that position, when the enemy's reply would cleave the neighbour, the AI places the new unit away from it.
- [ ] Two orders of the same moves into the same lanes still count as one position (the existing search tests pass).
- [ ] The lethal solver's results on the existing puzzles don't change.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, clippy, fmt and `cargo jackioh gate` pass.
- [ ] An improve-dev screen of 400 games against the parent build is reported in the pull request.

## Size and risks
Medium. Risks:
- More distinct open lines per level can crowd out other plays at `beam_width` 4; the cap guards against this.
- Decisions may get slower. Watch R977000's timing and the perf gate.
- The static evaluation alone can't tell lanes apart, so the gain depends on the reply's adjacency terms. The screen is what shows it.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-7` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40116918175)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

The beam's duplicate check in `beam_search_with` (`crates/ai/src/search.rs`) stops merging open lines whose positions differ only in which lanes their units stand in. Two orders of the same moves into the same lanes still count as one position. Each depth keeps at most `AI_SEARCH.zone_variants` open lines of one position up to its lanes, so lane variants that score alike can't fill `beam_width`. The lethal solver's visited set keeps today's `search_signature`, unchanged. Done looks like this: a search test shows a vanilla played away from its neighbour beside an enemy Cleaver, a `decide` test shows the AI's turn placing it there, every existing test and the checks are green, and an improve-dev screen of 400 games against the parent is reported.

## Files to touch

| Path | new/change | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/ai/src/simulate.rs` | change | new `pub fn unit_lanes`; `slot_of` import; `search_signature` doc |
| `crates/ai/src/search.rs` | change | `beam_search_with`'s `seen` key and lane-variant cap; imports; `beam_search` doc |
| `crates/ai/src/config.rs` | change | `AiSearch::zone_variants` doc: the cap and the screen's line |
| `crates/ai/tests/ai/search.rs` | change | `trace` import; `VANILLA`, `cleaver_board` and three tests in `mod lanes_that_play_differently` |
| `crates/ai/README.md` | change | one sentence after "(#1635)." (line 76) |

Do not touch: `crates/ai/src/lethal.rs`, `candidates.rs`, `reply.rs`, `evaluate.rs`, `crates/engine`, `crates/cards` (an AI change needs no patch fragment: #1801 and #1788 had none), `spec/`, `docs/polish/3-ai.md`, `training/`.

Governing spec: §9.9 (Search, The opponent's reply), §3.1 (lanes, adjacency), §4.4 step 10 and §6 Cleave (R63, priced by `reply.rs`'s `trade_value`). No ruling: this is how the search works, not a rules decision. Don't put a token like `r1797` in any test name, and don't cite any new R-id (`spec check`).

## Steps

0. **Build the parent first, before editing anything.** Run `cargo build --release -p jackioh-tools && cp target/release/jackioh /tmp/parent-jackioh`. That binary is base `633568b99`, which step 7 needs.

1. **`crates/ai/src/simulate.rs`, imports.** Add `slot_of` to the `use jackioh_engine::{…}` list. `PLAYER_IDS` and `active_units_of` are already there.

2. **`crates/ai/src/simulate.rs`, new function** directly after `search_signature`:

```rust
/// Every active unit's lane, each side's in `active_units_of` order, the sides in `PLAYER_IDS` order
/// (#1797): what `search_signature` leaves out. The beam's duplicate check reads the two together, so
/// two placements of one play that differ only in lane stay two positions, while two orders of the
/// same moves into the same lanes stay one.
pub fn unit_lanes(state: &GameState) -> String {
    PLAYER_IDS
        .into_iter()
        .map(|player| {
            active_units_of(state, player)
                .into_iter()
                .map(|unit| slot_of(state, unit).map_or(0, |slot| slot.lane).to_string())
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(",")
        })
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join("/")
}
```

   In `search_signature`'s doc, replace the last sentence ("A unit's lane is left out, so the two lanes `candidate_actions` keeps for one play stay one position.") with: "A unit's lane is left out, so the lethal solver's two lanes of one play stay one position; the beam reads it beside `unit_lanes` (#1797)." Leave the function body byte-identical.

3. **`crates/ai/src/search.rs`, imports.** Change `use indexmap::IndexSet;` to `use indexmap::{IndexMap, IndexSet};` and add `unit_lanes` to the `use crate::simulate::{…}` list.

4. **`crates/ai/src/search.rs`, `beam_search_with`.** Replace `let mut seen: IndexSet<String> = IndexSet::new();` with:

```rust
        // #1797: each open child's position with its units' lanes, and how many of those each position
        // without its lanes (`search_signature`) has kept.
        let mut seen: IndexSet<(String, String)> = IndexSet::new();
        let mut lane_variants: IndexMap<String, usize> = IndexMap::new();
```

   Then replace the comment and the five lines from `let signature = search_signature(&next, seat);` through `seen.insert(signature);` with:

```rust
                // Two orders of the same moves into the same lanes reach the same position: keep the
                // first, which ranks higher. Positions that differ only in where their units stand stay
                // apart (`unit_lanes`, #1797), so the placements the root tries reach the reply, but at
                // most AI_SEARCH.zone_variants of one position, the first in move order, so lane variants
                // that score alike cannot fill the beam.
                let placed = (search_signature(&next, seat), unit_lanes(&next));
                if seen.contains(&placed) {
                    continue;
                }
                let kept = lane_variants.entry(placed.0.clone()).or_insert(0);
                if *kept >= AI_SEARCH.zone_variants.max(1) as usize {
                    continue;
                }
                *kept += 1;
                seen.insert(placed);
```

   The exact-duplicate check comes before the cap, so a duplicate never counts toward it. Leave everything else in the loop alone: the scoring, the `stopped` path and the truncation to `beam_width`.

5. **`crates/ai/src/search.rs`, `beam_search` doc.** After "children whose status is not "open" become complete lines scored by terminalScore;", insert: "an open child whose position (`search_signature` with `unit_lanes`, #1797) an earlier child reached is dropped, as is one past the first `AI_SEARCH.zone_variants` of its position up to its units' lanes;".

6. **`crates/ai/README.md`, line 76.** After "…try the first `AI_SEARCH.zone_variants` (#1635).", add: "The beam drops an open line whose position an earlier one reached (two orders of the same moves are one position), but keeps apart positions that differ only in where their units stand, at most `AI_SEARCH.zone_variants` of each (#1797). So the placements the root tries reach the reply, which prices a Cleave into a unit's neighbours. The lethal solver's visited set still reads a position without its units' lanes."

7. **Tests** (below). Then run the screen: `cargo jackioh arena --a self --b bin:/tmp/parent-jackioh --set improve-dev --out /tmp/screen-1797`. It plays 400 games in 25 to 45 minutes, and the closing tally gives the wins, `edge`, `edgeLow` and `edgeHigh`.

8. **`crates/ai/src/config.rs`, `AiSearch::zone_variants` doc.** After "3 let a Tribute play's sets outgrow the lethal allowance.", append: "At each depth the beam keeps at most this many open lines of one position up to its units' lanes (#1797), so the placements the root tries reach the reply without lane variants that score alike filling `beam_width`; its screen, 400 games of improve-dev against the parent (`633568b99`), read W-L, edge E (LOW to HIGH)." Fill in the tally's numbers as the comments at `config.rs:96-97` and `candidates.rs:314-315` do. The value stays 2.

## Tests

All tests go in `crates/ai/tests/ai/search.rs`. Add `trace` to `use super::support::{AI, act, dealt_game, is_legal};`. Inside `mod lanes_that_play_differently`, after `mushroom_power_is_tried_between_its_units_in_lanes_3_and_5_at_the_root`, add:

```rust
    /// Mr. Vanilla, 4/4 with no text.
    const VANILLA: &str = "core-008";

    /// One of the AI's Mr. Vanillas in lane 1, another in its hand, and the enemy's Radiant Nurse
    /// Cleaver (classic-073, 6/12 Cleave) opposite lane 1. The vanilla's placements are lanes 2, 3 and 5
    /// (3 and 4 are one); only lane 2 is beside the unit, where the Cleaver's reply would kill both.
    fn cleaver_board() -> GameState {
        jackioh_cards::register_all();
        scenario(json!({
            "seed": "search-cleaver-lanes",
            "p1": { "hand": [VANILLA], "field": [{ "def": VANILLA, "lane": 1 }], "library": LIBRARY },
            "p2": { "field": [{ "def": "classic-073", "radiant": true, "lane": 1 }], "library": LIBRARY },
        }))
        .state()
        .clone()
    }
```

1. `two_orders_of_two_plays_into_the_same_lanes_are_one_position_and_another_lane_is_another`. A scenario with seed `"search-two-orders"` and `"p1": { "hand": [VANILLA, VANILLA], "library": LIBRARY }`, `"p2": { "library": LIBRARY }`, with `jackioh_cards::register_all()` first. Take the two hand ids (`state.players[AI].hand[0].id`, `[1].id`) and build plays with `body(json!({ "type": "play", "instanceId": id, "zone": { "row": "units", "lane": n } }))`: `a1` plays the first id into lane 1, and `b2` and `b3` play the second into lanes 2 and 3. Compute `one = act(&act(&state, AI, &a1), AI, &b2)`, `other = act(&act(&state, AI, &b2), AI, &a1)` and `apart = act(&act(&state, AI, &a1), AI, &b3)`. Assert:
   - `search_signature(&one, AI) == search_signature(&other, AI)` and `unit_lanes(&one) == unit_lanes(&other)`;
   - `search_signature(&one, AI) == search_signature(&apart, AI)`, because the lethal solver's signature stays lane-blind;
   - `unit_lanes(&one) != unit_lanes(&apart)`.

2. `the_beam_plays_a_vanilla_away_from_its_neighbour_and_opens_with_at_most_zone_variants_of_its_lanes`. Use `state = cleaver_board()`. First `assert_eq!(root_offered_lanes(&state, VANILLA), vec![2, 3, 5])`. Then `lines = beam_search(&state, AI, &create_node_counter(AI_BUDGET.nodes, None), AI_BUDGET)`. Assert:
   - Some line plays the vanilla into lane 3 or higher: `lines.iter().any(|line| lanes_of(&state, VANILLA, &line.actions).iter().any(|lane| *lane >= 3))`. This is the acceptance item.
   - No line opens with a lane past the cap: let `opening` be `lanes_of(&state, VANILLA, line.actions.get(..1).unwrap_or_default())` over every line. For each lane in `placements[AI_SEARCH.zone_variants as usize..]` (lane 5), assert `!opening.contains(lane)`.
   - The failure message prints every line's `action_key`s.

3. `decide_plays_a_vanilla_where_the_enemy_cleaver_cannot_splash_it_from_its_neighbour`. Use `state = cleaver_board()`, `vanilla = hand_id(&state, VANILLA)` and `neighbour = active_units_of(&state, AI)[0].id.clone()`. Run `turn = play_ai_turn(&state, AI, &mut ai_options("search-cleaver-lanes", AI_BUDGET))` and set `lane = |id: &str| find_instance(&turn.state, id).and_then(|card| slot_of(&turn.state, card)).map(|slot| slot.lane)`. Assert `lane(&neighbour) == Some(1)` and `lane(&vanilla).is_some_and(|lane| lane >= 3)`, with `trace(&turn)` as the message.

Prove the tests bite. Temporarily make `unit_lanes` return `String::new()`, run them, and confirm tests 1, 2 and 3 fail. Then put the body back.

Commands:
- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai lanes_that_play_differently`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`: every existing test, including `lethal.rs`, `puzzles.rs`, `position_model.rs` and R977000's in `match_.rs` and `shadow_ban.rs`
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo jackioh gate`, `cargo jackioh spec check`

## Done when

- [ ] Step 0's parent binary was built before any edit.
- [ ] `unit_lanes` exists and `search_signature`'s body is unchanged.
- [ ] The beam's `seen` key holds the lanes, with the cap at `AI_SEARCH.zone_variants`.
- [ ] The three new tests pass, and each failed with `unit_lanes` stubbed out.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` passes: the existing search, lethal and puzzle tests and R977000's.
- [ ] clippy, fmt, `cargo jackioh gate` and the harness's checks pass.
- [ ] The README, `beam_search` doc and `zone_variants` doc are updated, with the screen's real numbers.
- [ ] The final report gives the screen's tally line (wins, edge, edgeLow, edgeHigh, parent `633568b99`) for the pull request, and lists the decisions below.

Decisions to record in the report (each with the alternative rejected):
- Each unit's lane, not its own-side neighbours. It is simpler, and the backrow part of the signature is already positional.
- The cap applies as children are made, in move order, not after ranking. The two are the same while `open_score` reads no lane (`LEARNED_REACH` is `Finalists`, so it is `evaluate`, which reads none), and a capped child is never scored, so `own_prompt_score` spends no nodes on it.
- `AI_SEARCH.zone_variants` is reused rather than adding a new constant. Deeper levels already cap a play's lanes at it.
- The cap applies at every depth, not only the root.
- No ruling.
- `docs/polish/3-ai.md` is left alone, because its `beamSearch` sketch never described the duplicate check.

## Risks

- **Crowding.** Two lane variants of each of two plays can fill `beam_width` 4. The screen measures this. Don't tune the cap to improve the screen (`training/improve.md`, A screen, step 4).
- **Existing beam tests.** For example, `craft_a_cards_best_line_…` puts `beam_width` other plays beside Craft. If one fails, investigate; never loosen it. If it can't be fixed honestly, report it.
- **Determinism.** Use only `IndexMap` and `IndexSet` (`clippy.toml` bans hash-ordered collections), with no new randomness. A node costs the same: each frontier line expands the same number of moves.
- **The lethal solver.** It must not change. Leave `lethal.rs` alone and keep `search_signature` byte-identical; `lethal.rs`'s `two_one_step_children_with_one_signature_…` and `position_model.rs` hold it.
- **Hidden information.** `unit_lanes` reads only units on the field, which the redacted state shows (R185).
- **The decide test** depends on the reply attacking a Vanilla, not the face. It should: the kill is worth 8.8 by `unit_worth`, the face 6. If it plays elsewhere, print `trace` and the replied scores and work out why before changing the board. Never change the assertion.

## Open questions

- The issue sets no bar for the screen, and earlier AI patches shipped at edges near 0 (#1635 at -0.015). If `edgeHigh` comes out below 0, the builder still ships but puts that first in the report, so a person can decide whether to revert it.
